Attendees: Sofia Patel, Evan Kim, Lucia Alvarez, Daniel Cho, Priya Nair, Rajesh Menon, Maya Chen, Tom Reynolds, Hannah Lee, Omar Bashir, Leah Park

Summary:
Quick internal sync to review the incident from last week's canary rollout, validate launch readiness checklist items, and align on roadmap adjustments and runbook updates. Focus areas: root cause (autoscale + KV cache), perf regression on long-context LLMs, and communications plan.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and RCA hypotheses
- Autoscaler tuning and burst capacity behavior
- KV/prefix cache miss patterns and eviction policy impact
- QA signoffs, gating criteria for launch
- Security/audit log requirements (SOC2 notes)
- Next steps: postmortem, tests, runbook updates, exec summary

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Okay, let's get started. Thanks everyone for joining on short notice. We're here to go through the canary incident from last Thursday and then run through the launch readiness checklist, um, and make decisions on any roadmap slippage. I'll hand it to Rajesh to kick off with a short timeline.

[00:22] Rajesh Menon: Yeah thanks Sofia. Quick timeline: 2026-07-02 we deployed the new batching + KV eviction patch to canary (10% traffic). On 2026-07-07 at ~02:15 UTC we saw increased 95th and p99 latency for chat routes. Latency spiked from typical 120-180ms to 800ms+ on some long-context requests. Error rates rose slightly but not dramatically. We rolled back at 02:50 after mitigations.

[01:05] Evan Kim: I have the rough graphs, I'll drop them in the notes link — sorry the link is in the doc, it's in the meeting chat (link: https://redwood.internal/boards/canary-2026-07). We're seeing a KV cache thrash pattern correlated with autoscaler oscillations.

[01:42] Lucia Alvarez: To add, the eviction policy change moved from LRU-ish to a size-based heuristic, and that caused higher miss rates for long sequences. Misses meant more KV warming and longer latency while kernels rehydrated. Also our batching was more aggressive which increased seq length in some batches and amplified hotspotting.

[02:10] Tom Reynolds: One thing I noticed — the autoscaler cooldowns, the node tear-downs were too aggressive during the spike which chased the cache. So when nodes came back we had cold KV with a burst of requests. The autoscaler is configured with min nodes low for canary to save cost, which didn't help.

[02:45] Maya Chen: Right, so is the core cause autoscaler config + eviction heuristic + batching combined? Or is there a single root cause?

[03:05] Daniel Cho: It feels like an emergent property. Individually each change looked safe in load tests but under the real traffic distribution it pushed us over. The autoscaler reduction + more aggressive batching increased per-node memory pressure leading to the eviction heuristic firing. Once eviction starts, misses ripple out, causing higher latency and then autoscaler reacts, etc.

[03:38] Hannah Lee: QA saw a smaller regression in our synthetic suites but nothing like production. We need better long-tail synthetic scenarios.

[04:00] Sofia Patel: Ok let's capture that: test coverage gap for long-context traffic, autoscaler config too aggressive, eviction heuristic needs tuning, and batching policy might need to be workload-aware. Action items from that.

[04:20] Omar Bashir: On the security side, we looked at logs — audit logs are intact, no exfiltration. But the incident highlighted we need clearer SLO breach alerting and a playbook for cache-induced latency. Also we should document the KMS / key rotation steps used by private deploys in the runbook.

[04:50] Leah Park: From data/observability — I produced a first-pass KV cache heatmap; I'll share in the doc. It shows two hotspots where miss rates shoot during the spike windows.

[05:12] Evan Kim: I'm pasting the perf graph again. Note: there's a correlated CPU bump on GPU host side when miss rate spikes, which indicates more CPU orchestrating KV transfers. Could be a kernel selection or CPU scheduling issue.

[05:40] Sofia Patel: Do we have any immediate mitigations that are safe for prod? We rolled back the patch in canary; what about changing autoscaler cooldown or increasing min nodes temporarily?

[06:05] Daniel Cho: We can increase min nodes by 20% for the next 48 hours during any rollout windows. That's low risk. Also revert the eviction heuristic to the older LRU-ish policy while we tune.

[06:28] Rajesh Menon: Agreed. Those two mitigations buy us time. But for launch readiness we need concrete gating criteria so we don't ship with a latent risk.

[06:50] Sofia Patel: Let's go through the launch checklist: QA signoff, perf benchmarks, SLO targets, runbook, security review, cost projections, and canary duration.

[07:12] Maya Chen: QA signoff — currently failing long-context perf; not ready. We need targeted synthetic tests and a week of sustained canary traffic with the mitigations in place.

[07:35] Hannah Lee: I'll own the QA side. Plan: add long-context scenarios, run nightly regression and stress test for three days, then report. Estimated done by 2026-07-10.

[07:58] Sofia Patel: Perf benchmarks — we need a 95th percentile under the target for standard chat flows and acceptable degradation for >4k contexts. Also run the regression with 1M tokens to check amortized cost.

[08:22] Daniel Cho: I'll run the perf regression with targeted sequences — planning 1M tokens job; aim to finish by 2026-07-16. We'll confirm KV hit rate and kernel selection logs.

[08:45] Leah Park: Also suggest hooking in the tracing hooks from Redwood Console to see per-route token breakdowns. It helped in previous incident.

[09:02] Sofia Patel: Security review — Omar, are we good on SOC2/audit logs and SSO gating for the new feature?

[09:18] Omar Bashir: Audit logs are fine, but need to update the compliance doc with the new runbook steps around key rotation and private deployment KMS handling for the launch. I'll add that and share by 2026-07-12.

[09:40] Tom Reynolds: One open question — do we delay launch or proceed with cost of increasing baseline nodes? Finance will push back on extra spend.

[09:55] Rajesh Menon: If we delay two weeks we can be safer and lower risk, but that's a roadmap hit. If we keep date, we need a temporary reserved capacity bump and explicit cost acceptance.

[10:12] Priya Nair: From product ops — roadmap impact will cascade to the customer communications plan. We need to align on message either way.

[10:30] Sofia Patel: Let's assess risk tolerance. Rajesh, technical risk if we proceed with mitigations versus delay?

[10:46] Rajesh Menon: With mitigations (increased min nodes + revert eviction heuristic + tight monitoring) residual risk is moderate. There's still a chance of long-tail issues under unusual traffic. Delay reduces risk to low.

[11:05] Maya Chen: Stakeholder check — legal/compliance are okay, Sales ok but ask to avoid outages during initial rollout.

[11:20] Sofia Patel: Sounds like we have two options. I'll summarize later for execs. For immediate next steps: revert heuristic in staging/canary, increase min nodes temporarily, run the 1M token perf job, QA to expand long-context tests, update runbook, and prepare postmortem.

[11:40] Lucia Alvarez: Quick technical note — when reverting the eviction policy, we should also add a micro-benchmark to validate eviction behavior under controlled memory pressure.

[12:00] Daniel Cho: I'll add the autoscaler cooldown tweak and prepare the quick rollback patch.

[12:18] Hannah Lee: QA will schedule nightly runs and push results to the checklist doc.

[12:33] Sofia Patel: Anything else on roadmap adjustments? We might deprioritize a non-critical optimization in the next sprint to cover this work.

[12:50] Evan Kim: Yeah, the model quantization spike can be pushed by two sprints; engineering time will go into autoscaler + cache tuning.

[13:05] Rajesh Menon: Also flagging we need better canary isolation for critical infra changes; maybe separate canaries for infra vs user-facing changes.

[13:30] Sofia Patel: Agreed. We'll add a follow-up to review canary policy.

[13:42] Sofia Patel: Ok quick recap of tangible action items and owners — then we'll close.

[13:50] Sofia Patel: Rajesh to draft postmortem by 7/12; Lucia to produce KV heatmap and cache stats by 7/13; Daniel to validate autoscaler config and push patch by 7/11; Maya to update launch checklist by 7/10; Sofia to send exec summary and mitigation plan by 7/12. QA to run long-context tests and report by 7/10. Daniel to run 1M token perf job by 7/16.

[14:20] Tom Reynolds: Also linking the incident logs and runbook stub in chat: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-07-canary and https://redwood.internal/docs/runbook-2026-07

[14:35] Leah Park: I'll attach heatmaps and the initial trace breakdown in the folder.

[14:50] Sofia Patel: Great. Any final questions?

[15:00] Omar Bashir: One small ask — include the compliance contact in the postmortem email thread so audit gets notified.

[15:16] Priya Nair: Noted.

[15:25] Sofia Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene on the action items next week, and I'll update the execs after Rajesh's draft. Meeting adjourned.
